speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It is not just made up of Jalan Kayu private estate, which is the only area in Singapore with the name Jalan Kayu.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Jalan Kayu may be known for its prata and its eateries, but what not all of us may know about the constituency is that this is where you can find the last kampung on Singapore mainland, that is, Kampong Lorong Buangkok.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The only other kampung left in Singapore is on Pulau Ubin.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: Members can see from the URA Masterplan that Kampong Lorong Buangkok is the small little purple square that is now sitting on what is planned to be a highway and two schools.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: Is there really a need to displace the kampung residents, tear down the kampung in the name of urban redevelopment?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: Surely, we can explore ways where the kampung can co-exist and, in fact, enhance and bring value to urban life.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: Some have lived here for more than 50 years and would not live elsewhere even though their children are living in HDB estates and HDB flats and can house them comfortably in their flats.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: The neighbours all know one another very well, and each time I join my grassroots volunteers and residents there, the children visiting the kampung would have lots of fun chasing the kampung chickens, learning about the different fruit trees – rambutan, banana, noni, cocoa, you name it – and marveling at the homes that look like they are frozen in time in the 1960s.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: Our Jalan Kayu grassroots have done several community projects with the Kampong residents, one of which is the drain redevelopment project.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: Another one is where we gravelled the main entrance of the kampung and we put up signages for the kampung, because back then in the past, the only signage we could see was one that was handwritten in paint.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: This was me with Ms Sng, the landlady, and Members can see this is the new signage we put up a few months back.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: And the old name of the kampong was Kampong Selak Kain. "Selak kain" in Malay means you fold up your sarong or your kain – because in the past, the kampong always used to flood, that is why we did the drainage project; so, you selak your kain.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: These are some of the houses in the kampong; quite grand.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: I think this is the biggest house in the kampong out of the 26 available.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: It is two-storey, all made of wood, and this is what you can see in the kampong now.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: Members can see in the background that there are Build-To-Order (BTO) flats sprouting all over.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: The neighbours all know one another very well, and each time I join them, they will always be talking about how they want to continue living in the kampong and, even though some of the children may not want to live there, they want to retain the kampong for as long as possible.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: It is fascinating to see this kampong, which exemplifies racial and religious harmony.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: The kampong is owned by a Chinese lady, but the majority of the residents are Malay, living harmoniously with their Chinese neighbours.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: There is a Muslim surau, a small mosque, within the kampong, and there are altars that adorn the homes of the Chinese residents.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: Many of our Jalan Kayu residents have expressed their support to preserve the kampong, and one of them, a resident artist, Mr Vincent Seet, has held numerous exhibitions showing his numerous paintings of the kampong.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: These are some of the paintings by Mr Vincent Seet, a resident living in Buangkok HDB estate.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: I am also embarking on a community documentation and preservation project with my colleagues from the Singapore Institute of Technology to compile a photo-journal and oral history accounts of the residents living in the kampong, in a bid to preserve the experiences and memories of our residents who have lived there for many years, from before our Independence, to this day.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: The kampong can be integrated within the two schools that are planned under the URA masterplan.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: The kampong and its residents should be allowed to carry on their lives, but it can play the additional role of a community living lab for our students to learn about our shared history, culture and traditions, race relations, and experience for themselves values-in-action, such as communal living, the spirit of neighbourliness and community activism.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: In addition, our students can embark on community nature programmes to learn from and work with the residents on how they can grow plants and vegetables, or take care of animals, such as chickens, cats and dogs, in a more natural environment.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: On top of that, our kampong residents are exemplary in re-using and repurposing items in their farming and gardening methods.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: This is useful in helping our young ones be more environmentally friendly and increase their environmental awareness.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: I hope that the Ministry of Education can consider this, particularly in creating an authentic learning experience for values-in-action and for heritage and history education for our students.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: I understand there may be concerns regarding the maintenance and upkeep of the kampong.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: Singaporeans who are keen to experience what it is like to live in a kampung can do so here, as part of a resilience or community leadership training programme.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: So, instead of having overnight camps at PA or the Outward Bound campsites, this can be done at Kampong Lorong Buangkok in future.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: In addition, our own school children can have school leadership or training camps at Kampong Lorong Buangkok, too, for them to learn, to live with basic necessities, working and living with nature, and what the kampung spirit is all about.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: The second part of my speech is on the strip of green land parcel parallel to Gerald Drive, next to Seletar Springs condominium, that has been planned to be converted to a three-lane highway, which is known as Buangkok Drive extension.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: Many residents living along Gerald Drive and in Seletar Springs Condominium do not want this strip of land to be converted to a highway, citing a loss of natural flora and fauna.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: This is the actual strip of land that you can see from a height where the planned expressway or highway is supposed to be.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: As Members can see, this is really a green belt for both HDB and private estate residents living here.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: The strip of green is quite narrow and I can imagine that if URA were to proceed with the road construction here, the roads will come up close, very close to the HDB blocks and the private estates.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: I have had several dialogues with my Gerald-Mugliston residents to listen to their concerns and to assure them I will work closely with the Land Transport Authority (LTA) to ensure that only if the road is needed will it be built.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: Once gone, they are almost impossible to replace.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: We can, I suppose, create artificial green spaces or traditional setups to showcase our heritage, but they lack the character and soul of what has grown organically for many years.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: Once again, I iterate that I understand the need for urban development.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: Urban development and the preservation of green spaces and our places of heritage cannot be mutually exclusive.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: There are ways in which we can harmoniously integrate the two.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Kampong Lorong Buangkok is, as she has identified correctly, one of two remaining traditional kampungs left in Singapore, and the other is on Pulau Ubin.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Member may be aware of the work we are doing on Pulau Ubin, together with the Friends of Ubin Network, to enhance the rustic, nostalgic and authentic feel of the island.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This includes the heritage and the living community in the kampung.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In July this year, we launched the multi-year programme to restore and repair vacant kampung houses on the island and will be looking into how we can breathe new life into these returned homes.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We are also studying how we can work with the community to better support the villagers still living on the island.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, the Member will know where my personal inclinations lie on an issue such as this.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But for today's purposes, allow me to set out the position as it currently stands.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: It is regularly reviewed every five years to take into account the changing needs of Singaporeans, which may affect our future land use.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In the 2014 Master Plan, Kampong Lorong Buangkok straddles four land parcels.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: However, I must emphasise that there is no intention to implement these developments in the near future.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For instance, we will look into the need for the planned road only when we are ready to proceed with the longer-term development of Seletar.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This is likely to be several decades later.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And this must involve deep engagement with the kampong families living there at that time, to understand and consider their needs and interests.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Some may not want to move away from the kampong.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But they may also not want their community to be turned into an educational or heritage attraction, drawing crowds of curious visitors.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will also consider the wishes of Singaporeans who want the heritage and educational value of kampung life to be properly documented, retained and celebrated.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And yet, we cannot simply develop the surrounding areas around the kampong, isolating it from the rest of the community.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Indeed, kampung life can impart valuable lessons to Singaporeans about living together in gotong-royong.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We should all continue to foster and encourage this spirit of cooperation, bonding, neighbourliness and mutual help in our community.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: MND has considered the Member’s proposal in consultation with the relevant agencies.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This road will serve as a vital connection across Sungei Punggol and help relieve potential traffic congestion problems for Singaporeans living there in Sengkang and Hougang Towns, where the existing road network cannot support the higher resident population in the future.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Moreover, there is already a provision of green space for residents in and around Gerald Drive, including existing HDB common greens and neighbourhood parks.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Park Connector Network also runs along Sungei Punggol, linking the Gerald Drive area to Sengkang Riverside Park, which is a large town park.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: If she has further queries or concerns, she can raise them to us, and we will get URA and all relevant agencies to take her through the plans in detail.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Is there anything you would like to raise?
